instructions: You are one of two independent readers for a public record that scores theories of consciousness. Read the prediction, the wording of what would count for and against it, and the passages from the study. Decide whether this study's result is FOR the prediction, AGAINST it, or MIXED (parts for and parts against, or a result that cannot tell the two apart). Judge only from the material given; if you rely on anything else, say what. Answer in JSON: {"verdict": "for"|"against"|"mixed", "reason": "two to four plain sentences", "unsure": true|false, "unsure_why": "what would change your answer, or empty"}.

core_claim.quote: The prefrontal cortex is posited to play a key role in the GNW because of the greater density of neurons thought to be critical for global broadcasting of information, but it is not proposed as the exclusive territory for conscious access.

source.citation: Mashour GA, Roelfsema P, Changeux J-P, Dehaene S. Conscious processing and the global neuronal workspace hypothesis. Neuron 105(5):776-798, 2020

prediction.statement: What is consciously seen is represented in prefrontal cortex, so that its content can be decoded there, whether or not the person has to report it or use it in a task.

first_stated.passage: Global information sharing and routing would rely on a set of interconnected high-level cortical regions forming a ‘global workspace’ and involving primarily the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, but also additional hubs in inferior parietal cortex, mid-temporal cortex, and precuneus

source.citation: Dehaene S, Charles L, King J-R, Marti S. Toward a computational theory of conscious processing. Current Opinion in Neurobiology 25:76-84, 2014

prediction.test_for: Features of a stimulus that the person consciously sees (its category, orientation, identity) can be decoded from prefrontal activity, including when the stimulus or the feature is irrelevant to the task and nothing is reported.
prediction.test_against: A feature the person consciously sees can be decoded from sensory cortex but not from prefrontal cortex, in a design sensitive enough to find it in prefrontal cortex for other features.

study.name: Decoding rapidly presented pictures from monkey prefrontal neurons without report

source.citation: Bellet J, Gay M, Dwarakanath A, Jarraya B, van Kerkoerle T, Dehaene S, Panagiotaropoulos TI. Decoding rapidly presented visual stimuli from prefrontal ensembles without report nor post-perceptual processing. Neuroscience of Consciousness 2022(1):niac005

passages.text: We report that the identity of each stimulus could be decoded from PFC population activity even in the RSVP condition.

source.citation: Bellet J, Gay M, Dwarakanath A, Jarraya B, van Kerkoerle T, Dehaene S, Panagiotaropoulos TI. Decoding rapidly presented visual stimuli from prefrontal ensembles without report nor post-perceptual processing. Neuroscience of Consciousness 2022(1):niac005

passages.text: Due to the lack of subjective report under the present RSVP conditions, two interpretations of the data remain tenable: macaques could either be very fast in perceiving the stimuli or most of the stimuli could have remained unconscious.

source.citation: Bellet J, Gay M, Dwarakanath A, Jarraya B, van Kerkoerle T, Dehaene S, Panagiotaropoulos TI. Decoding rapidly presented visual stimuli from prefrontal ensembles without report nor post-perceptual processing. Neuroscience of Consciousness 2022(1):niac005

passages.text: The main limitation of the present study is the absence of behavioral reports that could have provided insight as to whether any of the signals we have decoded are correlates of consciousness.

source.citation: Bellet J, Gay M, Dwarakanath A, Jarraya B, van Kerkoerle T, Dehaene S, Panagiotaropoulos TI. Decoding rapidly presented visual stimuli from prefrontal ensembles without report nor post-perceptual processing. Neuroscience of Consciousness 2022(1):niac005
